primitives.name: Expected Points Added and Win Probability Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: **WHAT IT IS:** The original R package for scraping NFL play-by-play from NFL.com GameCenter JSON and computing EPA/WP — the direct ancestor of nflfastR/
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EPA': 'expected points added, dimensionless', 'WP': 'win probability, unitless in [0,1]', 't': 'time in game, seconds', 's': 'score differential, points'}
primitives.assumptions: Game state transitions follow Markov process; EPA/WP computed from historical play outcomes and game metadata.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When game state exceeds historical training coverage (e.g., extreme score differentials or time remaining).

layer2.mapping: EPA/WP serve as kernel functions for GSE's state-action value estimation in play-calling optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of EPA predictions vs. actual scoring events; WP convergence to final game outcome.

primitives.name: Sports Reference Data Scraper
primitives.verbatim_quote: **WHAT IT IS:** Python library and CLI that scrapes Sports Reference sites (Pro Football Reference for NFL) into typed datasets: teams, rosters, schedules, boxscores, players.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'team identifier, categorical', 'P': 'player identifier, categorical', 'S': 'schedule entry, timestamp', 'B': 'boxscore data, structured table'}
primitives.assumptions: Data integrity preserved through consistent site structure; scraping adheres to rate limits and terms of service.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Sports Reference updates schema or enforces anti-bot measures.

layer2.mapping: Maps PFR data structures to GSE's internal relational schema for player/team modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency of scraped fields with known PFR data formats; API availability.
